en: Itivuttaka 9: Ekakanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the venerable Ānanda. The venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying this: 'Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; I shall reveal the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure. Now, friends, what is that Dhamma that the Blessed One has taught, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and which he has revealed as the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure? When this was said, the venerable Ānanda spoke thus to the bhikkhus: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying this: 'Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; I shall reveal the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure.

Now, friends, what is that Dhamma that the Blessed One has taught, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and which he has revealed as the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure? Friends, it is this one thing: the mind. For the mind, friends, is the forerunner of all wholesome qualities; the mind arises first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Just as, friends, when a skilled turner or his apprentice, having applied his attention to a single piece of wood, turns it around, that piece of wood follows after his mind; even so, friends, the mind is the forerunner of all wholesome qualities; the mind arises first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Therefore, friends, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will guard our minds well; we will protect our minds well; we will fulfill the development of the mind. It is in this way, friends, that you should train yourselves. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda spoke thus to the bhikkhus: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying this: 'Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; I shall reveal the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure. Now, friends, what is that Dhamma that the Blessed One has taught, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and which he has revealed as the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure? Friends, it is this one thing: mindfulness directed to the body. For mindfulness directed to the body, friends, is the forerunner of all wholesome qualities; mindfulness directed to the body arises first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Just as, friends, when a skilled turner or his apprentice, having applied his attention to a single piece of wood, turns it around, that piece of wood follows after his mind; even so, friends, mindfulness directed to the body is the forerunner of all wholesome qualities; mindfulness directed to the body arises first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Therefore, friends, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will develop mindfulness directed to the body; we will cultivate mindfulness directed to the body; we will make mindfulness directed to the body our vehicle; we will make mindfulness directed to the body our foundation; we will establish mindfulness directed to the body well. It is in this way, friends, that you should train yourselves. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda spoke thus to the bhikkhus: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying this: 'Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; I shall reveal the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure. Now, friends, what is that Dhamma that the Blessed One has taught, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and which he has revealed as the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure? Friends, it is this one thing: the four foundations of mindfulness. For the four foundations of mindfulness, friends, are the forerunners of all wholesome qualities; the four foundations of mindfulness arise first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Just as, friends, when a skilled turner or his apprentice, having applied his attention to a single piece of wood, turns it around, that piece of wood follows after his mind; even so, friends, the four foundations of mindfulness are the forerunners of all wholesome qualities; the four foundations of mindfulness arise first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Therefore, friends, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will develop the four foundations of mindfulness; we will cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness; we will make the four foundations of mindfulness our vehicle; we will make the four foundations of mindfulness our foundation; we will establish the four foundations of mindfulness well. It is in this way, friends, that you should train yourselves. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda spoke thus to the bhikkhus: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying this: 'Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; I shall reveal the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure. Now, friends, what is that Dhamma that the Blessed One has taught, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and which he has revealed as the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure? Friends, it is this one thing: the four right strivings. For the four right strivings, friends, are the forerunners of all wholesome qualities; the four right strivings arise first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Just as, friends, when a skilled turner or his apprentice, having applied his attention to a single piece of wood, turns it around, that piece of wood follows after his mind; even so, friends, the four right strivings are the forerunners of all wholesome qualities; the four right strivings arise first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Therefore, friends, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will generate desire for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; we will make an effort, arouse energy, apply our minds, and strive. We will generate desire for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; we will make an effort, arouse energy, apply our minds, and strive. We will generate desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; we will make an effort, arouse energy, apply our minds, and strive. We will generate desire for the maintenance of arisen wholesome states, for their non-decline, increase, expansion, and fulfillment through cultivation; we will make an effort, arouse energy, apply our minds, and strive. It is in this way, friends, that you should train yourselves. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda spoke thus to the bhikkhus: "Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and entered his dwelling after saying this: 'Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; I shall reveal the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure. Now, friends, what is that Dhamma that the Blessed One has taught, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, and which he has revealed as the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure? Friends, it is this one thing: the four bases of psychic power. For the four bases of psychic power, friends, are the forerunners of all wholesome qualities; the four bases of psychic power arise first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Just as, friends, when a skilled turner or his apprentice, having applied his attention to a single piece of wood, turns it around, that piece of wood follows after his mind; even so, friends, the four bases of psychic power are the forerunners of all wholesome qualities; the four bases of psychic power arise first, and then wholesome qualities follow. Therefore, friends, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will develop the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving; we will make an effort, arouse energy, apply our minds, and strive. We will develop the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration due to energy and volitional formations of striving
The Discourse on the Full Understanding of Greed.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, one who has not directly known greed, who has not fully understood it, and who has not detached the mind from it and abandoned it, is incapable of the destruction of suffering."
“Monks, by directly knowing and fully understanding greed, and by causing the mind to fade away from it and abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. Regarding this, it is said:
“Having fully understood that greed by which beings, being greedy, go to an evil destination— ”
Those who possess insight abandon them;
having abandoned them, they never again return to this world.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
